integrator_questions: Did line_loss_events fall on the s-bend and slalom with the 60 mm span at y = 0.075 m, and where does the first loss occur on each track?
Does max_error drop below 0.06 on the s-bend and slalom, or does the robot still leave the track at the same bend?
Does rms_error or steering_oscillation rise with the wider span (the signal may be less sensitive near the centre)? Does kd still damp it?
If line loss is 0 but the robot still leaves the track, is the limit wheel-command saturation (+/-4095) or control response?
What is completion_time on the oval finishes, and is there speed margin to raise base_speed toward 1.5 m/s average?

intent: Kept y = 0.075 m, five sensors, the 12 mm footprint, the 0.12 m track, the 0.03 m wheels, the 0.6 kg mass and the 0.12 m body width from iteration 4. Changed only the sensor span, from 50 mm to 60 mm (x = ±0.03 m), following the advance rule for line loss at the forward limit. I expect line_loss_events to fall below 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom and max_error to drop below 0.06 on at least some bends, with a score above 291.9. I am considering, without committing, narrowing wheel_track to about 0.10 m for more turn rate, but only if line loss reaches 0 and max_error stays at or above 0.06.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) the remaining s-bend and slalom losses come from the tape leaving the outer sensors on sharp bends, so a 60 mm span keeps it in view; (2) once line loss clears, the binding limit is turning authority, which a narrower wheel_track should relieve; (3) the wider span will add modest signal jitter but not destabilise the loop. Measurements requested per track: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort. line_loss_events separates sensor coverage from control, and max_error shows whether drift still reaches the off-track limit.
rationale: Iteration 4 (array at y = 0.075 m, 50 mm span) is the best design so far at 291.9. The oval finished 15 of 20 runs (mean progress 0.81, max_error 0.041), so forward placement worked there. The s-bend and slalom still ended off track in all 40 runs, with line_loss_events at 2.0 on both and max_error at 0.072 and 0.066. Line loss is still at least 1 on every track, so the rule the Integrator and I set in advance now applies: keep the array at y = 0.075 m, which is the top of the forward range, and widen the span to x = ±0.03 m (60 mm). I am following that advice. The forward array has been run to its limit, and the span is the variable that has moved coverage in earlier iterations (iteration 0 to 1 cut line loss on the oval), so I change only the span. I keep five sensors, the 12 mm footprint, the 0.12 m wheel track, the 0.03 m wheels, the 0.6 kg mass and the 0.12 m body width. Body width still does not affect the 0.06 m off-track floor, and mass and track are not yet shown to limit the outcome. Sensor spacing becomes 15 mm, so adjacent footprints still overlap. Expected result: line_loss_events falls below 2.0 on the s-bend and slalom, the robot holds the line through the tight bends, and the score exceeds 291.9. Risk: a wider span may reduce signal sensitivity on the centre line, so steering_oscillation and rms_error are the watch points. If line loss clears but max_error stays at or above 0.06, the next lever is narrowing wheel_track to about 0.10 m.
